reason: No existing skill covers proving a module-table, store-version or upgrade-path change on planted stores with old and new code side by side. The episode built exactly that proof by hand (HEAD copy vs working tree, planted version 14, conflict via retype) and hit several pitfalls worth keeping at the class level.

Ticket 13b34894 showed the store comparison missed CHECK, foreign key, unique/partial index and collation differences, and that a constraint change without a version raise slipped through; the worker also hit the sqlite_autoindex naming crash. This skill is the one the worker was running under and it only covers columns and index lists.
The description missed the trigger a user or agent hits when a live store is upgraded underneath running processes: the error text "schema version" is what surfaces, not the word "schema change".

A peer agent raised the live store to schema 22 while the web GUI, MCP server and runners still ran code that reads only 21, so their writes were refused. The skill proves changes on planted copies but says nothing about the live rollout or about processes that were started before the bump.

The existing rule was correct but did not reach the worker: the ticket said copy-first and the agent migrated live anyway, leaving running processes unable to write. The skill should say what to do when a worker breaks the rule.
